name: a5r
description: A5R (Agent 5 Rules): Hai's S2 flow beside Ather Automata, which it never changes. A5R off: Ather exactly as it ships (decisions are Ather's: A5R has no decision convention of its own). /a5r on: the five rules (D9), checked at the action only for what cannot be undone, on facts and never by a dialog (A5R never asks or waits; it runs a call or refuses it with an alternative) and at A5R acceptance only at the end of the checklist (a PR through gh or an MCP tool once every row of the tracked intent is met or waived, Ather's Ship prompt, an intent close, and after the fact for a PR listed then; it never asks: a failing score refuses with its list and /a5r pass lets one through; a card in the A5R pane); every Editor lease leaves one record (Saved/A5R/leases.jsonl) with a 24-hour summary and the queue on the panel, a working holder is never told to release for idleness, a retest extends the same slot, a holder is asked to yield only between Editor work and a forced release keeps its place; a lapsed Editor lease is released only when its session is gone and no Editor or build runs, a grant its session never saw passes on, every such event is logged to Saved/A5R/orchestrate.log, and no grant is made over a merge, revert or cherry-pick in progress; an advisory judge (a read-only background agent, one per incident) reads a stalled holder's facts and transcript tail and shows its verdict on an Orchestrate card, changing nothing; title marks clear when Hai types, after a reload too, and coordination for the sessions sharing one S2 checkout: Editor holder (queue, leases, the S2 standard's lock lines), RAM (safe cleanup, launch and PIE gates), Sync main holder (cutoff, a freeze that is a lease with a hard end, a sync worker that runs the merge without a5r tools (the holder's a5r takes and releases the Editor lock and reads its SYNC MERGED or SYNC ABORT line; an abort hands the sync back to its holder, still frozen, with the Editor lock and the holder's conflict rules), the merge guard (MERGE_HEAD, REVERT_HEAD, CHERRY_PICK_HEAD: only the operation's owner writes), conflicts to their owners), with a5r notices that never enter intent files, one compact A5R line of icons and values in Ather's pane (★ A5R › on seal red) and an A5R pane of its own (/a5r, all in English): a thin seal-red band, one tools list, one Editor list (the holder, then the queue in the order every session computes, with plain reasons and a day's line), the other sessions, the acceptance card, NEEDS A LOOK only when a stalled holder needs the person, and five rule chips that open a card each; the person alone (a panel press or his own /a5r editor command, never a tool) rearranges the Editor queue and gives a turn more time, through the shared Saved/A5R/queue-order.json; offers a Focus to a lane that keeps coming back and shows an overrun with people waiting with his release in NEEDS A LOOK; closes an Editor left by a gone session gracefully (one WM_CLOSE to that PID, only when it is certainly orphaned); plans a merge-only sync of main by itself when none ran for 6 h, through the sync conductor session; counts only live waits; and gives one session a Focus (a panel press or his own /a5r focus command, Saved/A5R/editor-focus.json): the Editor for a 30-min to 3-h box toward a milestone, kept through closes, builds and reopens, ended by the session's focus done, by the person or by the box end only, with the other sessions' turns re-planned behind it and their launches, shared-project builds and Editor writes refused meanwhile; one-shot pixel dithers on the desktop.

a5rWhenPresent.title: A5R approvals (unused since 0.15.0)
a5rWhenPresent.description: Kept for old settings files; unused since 0.15.0: A5R never asks and never waits at the action (A73). A call runs, or is refused with what to do instead, on measured facts; bypass mode and an away window give the same answers.

editorLock.title: Editor owner lock file (per machine, optional)
editorLock.description: The shared Unreal checkout's lock, <checkout>/Saved/EDITOR_OWNER.txt (AGENTS.md), set in your own settings for this machine. Unset: A5R finds the checkout from the session's own git repository: its main working tree (a worktree leads to it) when that tree holds a .uproject at its root. A session outside any such checkout keeps the five rules; its coordination (Editor, Sync main, the queue on the panel) is idle and says to set this option. Set it when sessions outside the checkout must coordinate on it too.

motion.title: Pixel motion in Ather's pane
motion.description: on: a tile's pixel icon dithers in when its state turns over, the Branch icon sweeps while a sync runs, the A5R seal stamps in, the A5R pane's blocks dither in from red pixels when it opens (within 0.3 s) and events dither once; slow: the same, with the pane's entrance and the event dithers ten times slower (about 3 s), for checking the animations on the real pane; off: every icon stays still.

launchGatePieGb.title: A5R Editor launch gate, slot with PIE (GB free)
launchGatePieGb.description: Free RAM, after the safe cleanup, a slot with PIE needs before the Editor is launched (an Editor already open is reused). 38 since 0.21.0: a MainChar PIE needed 37-38 GB free before launch on the machine it was measured on. /a5r gate <with PIE> <without PIE> moves it for every session; /a5r gate reset returns to this value. The PIE gate itself (start at 5 GB, abort under 3 GB) is fixed.

launchGateGb.title: A5R Editor launch gate, slot without PIE (GB free)
launchGateGb.description: Free RAM, after the safe cleanup, a slot without PIE needs before the Editor is launched.

syncMergeMinutes.title: A5R Sync main: freeze length for a merge (minutes)
syncMergeMinutes.description: The freeze from the sync time is a lease: past this many minutes without done or abort the sync expires, git and the Editor open again for every session, and every session is told.

syncBuildMinutes.title: A5R Sync main: freeze length for a merge with a build (minutes)
syncBuildMinutes.description: The same hard end for a sync planned with a build (/a5r sync HH:MM build, or Build: on in the panel's Sync ⋯ dialog).

editorLaunchers.title: A5R: your own Editor launcher scripts (optional)
editorLaunchers.description: Script names (comma-separated, for example launch_s2.ps1) whose run starts an Unreal Editor, set in your own settings for the projects that have them. A5R then treats running one as an Editor launch (it needs the Editor lock, and while another session has a Focus it is refused). Unset: no script name is read as a launch (only UnrealEditor itself, Start-Process of it, and the probe).

pieDrivers.title: A5R: your own PIE driver scripts (optional)
pieDrivers.description: Python script names (comma-separated, for example lab.py) whose run plays PIE in the Editor, set in your own settings for the projects that have them. A5R then records PIE for the lease (pieAt, and the 3 GB PIE abort) when the probe sees one run, as it does for an Unreal PIE window and for PIE started through Unreal MCP; and an Editor is never closed as orphaned while one runs. Unset: no script name is read as PIE.

autoSyncBuild.title: A5R Sync main: auto-planned syncs build
autoSyncBuild.description: Whether a sync A5R plans by itself (when none ran for 6 h) includes the build, with the longer freeze (syncBuildMinutes). On by default (Hai, 2026-10-29: a sync must build, or nobody knows it has no errors); off: an auto-planned sync is merge-only (syncMergeMinutes, 45). A sync planned by hand chooses for itself as before.

engineRoot.title: A5R Sync main: engine root for the sync's build (per machine, optional)
engineRoot.description: The Unreal engine root whose Engine\Build\BatchFiles\Build.bat builds the checkout, set in your own settings for this machine to override what A5R finds. Unset: A5R takes the engine the checkout's Editor last ran with (the newest Saved/Logs/<project>.log line 'LogInit: Base Directory:'), else the .uproject's EngineAssociation in Epic's registry entries; a root counts only when its Build.bat exists. Written into the sync's build script (Saved/A5R/<sync id>-build.cmd), which the sync worker starts with one command; with no root found no script is written and the holder is told to set this option or build by hand.
